tone_statements.citation: Starostin, George (comp. and annot.). 2017. Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the Karen group (Sino-Tibetan family). The Global Lexicostatistical Database (GLD), Moscow. Languages incl. Brek Kayaw [krn-bre]; last update June 2017.
tone_statements.quote: The transcription system used in [Myar 2004], our main source on lexical data for Kayah Monu, Brek Kayaw, and Yintale, is largely IPA-compatible [...] Tones are represented with tone letters in the source, recoded to UTS diacritics. The typical four-way opposition (Kayah Monu, Brek Kayaw) is high (marked as V̋), high-mid (marked as V́), mid (marked as V̄), and low (marked as V̀). Additionally, Yintale also has contour tones (rising V̌, falling V̂)

tone_statements.citation: Luangthongkum, Theraphan. 2014. Karenic as a Branch of Tibeto-Burman: More Evidence from Proto-Karen. Paper presented at SEALS24, Department of Myanmar Language, University of Yangon and SOAS, Yangon, Myanmar, May 27-31, 2014. 12 pp.
tone_statements.quote: The elicited data obtained from ten Karen languages and/or their varieties was transcribed using IPA symbols. The minute and unnecessary phonetic differences were eliminated for the sake of a generalisation of the consonant, vowel and tone systems in each Karenic language variety before searching for cognates. For example, the high tones, mid tones and low tones were specified as 55, 33 and 11, respectively, no matter what the detailed phonetic characteristics of these three tones were. As for the contour tones, the more common ones are the falling tones, i.e. 53 or 31. [...] Kayan, E.Kayah, W.Bwe (Henderson's Blimaw) and Kayaw for Central Karen (CK)

tone_statements.quote: Taking the Karen Tone Box and applying it to Karen language varieties shows a number of striking patterns (Table 2): the top two rows prototone *B´ merged with prototone *C; all languages except Pwo had a 2-way split [fn. 1: Palaychi also had a 3-way split, but has yet to be included in the analysis.]; breathy phonation is associated with protovoiced initial consonants; closed syllables with non-voiced initials are either high (5) or mid (3) tone [...] Table 2: Tone Boxes for Karen languages
tone_statements.locator: (section 'Tone patterns', bulleted list) and (Table 2, tone boxes for Kayaw, Kayan, Bwe-Geba, Kayah, Yintale, Yinbaw, Paku, Manu, Sgaw, Pa'O, Pwo; Kayaw box legible cells 5 1 3 3 / 5 1 3 3); 'Kayaw and Manu form a cluster'

tone.says: Applies Manson's Karen Tone Box (after Kauffman 1993) to Karen varieties; Table 2 prints a tone box for Kayaw with pitch values 5, 3 and 1 in the legible cells; generalisations: prototone *B' merged with *C, all languages except Pwo had a two-way tone split, closed syllables with non-voiced initials are high (5) or mid (3); tonal development is used as a subgrouping criterion.
